name: Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Survey on Agentic RAG (Singh et al.)
venue: arXiv preprint (arXiv:2501.09136, cs.AI/cs.CL/cs.IR). Submitted 15 Jan 2025 (v1); revised through v4 on 1 Apr 2026. Not a peer-reviewed venue; arXiv-issued DOI 10.48550/arXiv.2501.09136. As of indexing it is a widely cited preprint (Semantic Scholar reports 311 citations).
authors_affiliation: Aditi Singh (Department of Computer Science, Cleveland State University, Cleveland, OH, USA); Abul Ehtesham (Kent State University, Kent, OH, USA); Saket Kumar (Khoury College of Computer Science, Northeastern University, Boston, MA, USA); Tala Talaei Khoei (Khoury College, Roux Institute at Northeastern University, Portland, ME, USA); Athanasios V. Vasilakos (Center for AI Research, University of Agder (UiA), Grimstad, Norway). Five authors; multiple US universities plus University of Agder (Norway).
code_url: N/A (this is a survey; the authors provide no official code/implementation repository. The many github.com links in the paper are citations to third-party frameworks such as LangChain/LangGraph, LlamaIndex, CrewAI, AG2/AutoGen, and OpenAI Swarm, not an artifact of the survey.)
maintained_repo_url: N/A (no continuously-updated authors' paper list or leaderboard repository is associated with this survey; the work is a frozen PDF that the authors revise on arXiv, most recently to v4 on 1 Apr 2026.)
task_domain: Survey / taxonomy. Surveys Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation (Agentic RAG): RAG pipelines augmented with autonomous LLM agents. Spans QA (single-hop, multi-hop, long-form, domain-specific), multi-step reasoning, tool-use, web search, document-centric workflows, and decision-making; it reviews applications in customer support, healthcare/personalized medicine, legal/contract analysis, finance/risk, education, and enterprise document processing rather than a single task domain.
problem_setting: This is an analytical literature survey, not a method or system with original experiments. It traces the evolution of RAG paradigms (Naive RAG -> Advanced RAG -> Modular RAG -> Graph RAG -> Agentic RAG), defines the agentic design patterns (reflection, planning, tool use, multi-agent collaboration) and agentic workflow patterns (prompt chaining, routing, parallelization, orchestrator-workers, evaluator-optimizer), and proposes a principled taxonomy of Agentic RAG architectures. It covers both single- and multi-agent settings and interactive/iterative workflows as surveyed sub-areas, but the survey itself defines no controlled experimental protocol, training supervision, or benchmark of its own; it provides comparative (qualitative) analysis tables and distilled practitioner lessons.
what_is_retrieved: N/A as an artifact (the survey itself retrieves nothing). As surveyed content, Agentic RAG systems retrieve: documents/passages (unstructured docs, PDFs, organizational records via vector/semantic search), structured/tabular data (via Text-to-SQL over PostgreSQL/MySQL), real-time web search results, recommendation-engine outputs, knowledge-graph subgraphs (Graph-based Agentic RAG, e.g., Agent-G, GeAR), tools/APIs, and agent memory (prior context across multi-step workflows).
retrieval_grounding: Survey-level: covers BOTH access to STATIC/dynamic external corpora (document stores, structured databases, web search, knowledge graphs, APIs) and a GROWING agent memory (memory modules that maintain state/context across multi-step workflows). The survey frames retrieval as dynamically managed by agents (HYBRID across structured DBs, unstructured docs, web, KGs); it itself is grounded in no single corpus.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: N/A (survey; defines no retrieval objective of its own). Surveyed Agentic RAG emphasizes adaptive, agent-controlled retrieval (e.g., Corrective RAG re-retrieving when relevance is low; Adaptive RAG selecting no-retrieval / single-step / multi-step based on query complexity) rather than a single fixed top-k vs completeness objective. It notes retrieval quality/coverage as the primary bottleneck but proposes no completeness metric.
cbr_cycle_coverage: N/A (the survey is not a case-based reasoning system and implements no Retrieve/Reuse/Revise/Retain cycle).
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The survey does not frame Agentic RAG as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner; it organizes the field around agentic design patterns (reflection, planning, tool use, multi-agent) and an architecture taxonomy (agent cardinality, control structure, autonomy, knowledge representation).
retrieval_unit: N/A (survey defines no single retrieval unit). Surveyed units span: document/passage (semantic/vector retrieval over PDFs and records), table rows/structured records (Text-to-SQL), web pages/snippets (web search), knowledge-graph subgraphs / node-edge structures (Graph-based Agentic RAG: Agent-G, GeAR, GNN-RAG), tools/APIs, and memory entries (state across multi-step document workflows).
index_source: N/A for the survey. Surveyed Agentic RAG draws on static/dynamic external stores (vector indexes over documents, SQL databases, live web search, knowledge graphs) combined with a growing agent memory written during multi-step workflows; the survey builds no index itself. It explicitly notes that poorly constructed indexes are a common failure source.
index_structure_topology: N/A (survey has no index of its own). It reviews multiple store organizations used by Agentic RAG: flat vector indexes (dense/sparse, e.g., Qdrant switching sparse<->dense), structured relational databases (Text-to-SQL over PostgreSQL/MySQL), and knowledge GRAPHS (Graph-based Agentic RAG -- Agent-G, GeAR, GNN-RAG -- enabling relational/multi-hop reasoning). Its taxonomy lists knowledge representation as unstructured vs unstructured-or-hybrid vs graph-based/document-centric.
retriever_type: N/A (survey; no retriever implemented). Surveyed retrievers include dense/embedding-based semantic search, sparse vector search, hybrid sparse+dense (e.g., Qdrant adaptive switching), Text-to-SQL query generation, web-search APIs, and graph neural retrieval (GNN-RAG). LLM agents act as query routers/reformulators (LLM-as-controller of retrieval) rather than as the retriever.
retriever_learning_signal: N/A (survey; trains no retriever). It reviews systems where retrieval is controlled by LLM agents using prompting, query reformulation, reflection, and learned query-complexity classifiers (Adaptive RAG uses a classifier to route queries), and relevance-evaluation agents (Corrective RAG) rather than a contrastively trained retriever; it proposes no learning signal of its own.
query_construction: N/A (survey). Surveyed Agentic RAG constructs queries via agent-driven query reformulation/refinement (Corrective RAG's Query Refinement Agent), self-query, decomposition for multi-hop reasoning, and routing by a coordinating/master retrieval agent that selects knowledge sources based on query type; the survey prescribes no single query-construction method.
query_granularity: N/A (survey). Surveyed systems range from task-level routing (single-agent router at intake) to iterative step/sub-query-level construction (multi-step reasoning, corrective re-querying); Adaptive RAG selects granularity by query complexity. The survey commits to no single granularity.
when_to_retrieve: N/A (survey). Surveyed Agentic RAG spans one-shot, iterative, and adaptive retrieval: Corrective RAG retrieves iteratively/correctively when document relevance is low; Adaptive RAG uses a learned query-complexity classifier to decide between no-retrieval, single-step, and multi-step retrieval (adaptive/learned router); single-agent router decides per query.
retrieval_trigger_signal: N/A (survey defines no single trigger). Surveyed triggers include: a learned query-complexity classifier (Adaptive RAG), a relevance-evaluation agent comparing retrieved documents to a relevance threshold (Corrective RAG), and agent-initiated reflection/planning loops. The survey reviews these rather than standardizing one.
reranking: N/A (survey; no reranking stage of its own). It situates reranking within the Advanced RAG paradigm (pre-/post-retrieval optimization including re-ranking) and within Corrective RAG's relevance evaluation, but contributes no reranking method itself.
retrieved_context_refinement: N/A (survey). It reviews refinement operations used by Agentic RAG: relevance evaluation and filtering of retrieved documents, query refinement/reformulation, corrective re-retrieval from external sources when context is insufficient (Corrective RAG), and iterative refinement of context across reflection loops; it implements no refinement pipeline itself.
tool_document_engineering: N/A (survey contributes no tool-document-engineering technique). It discusses tool use as a core agentic pattern and reviews frameworks (LangChain, LlamaIndex, CrewAI, AG2/AutoGen, Semantic Kernel, OpenAI Swarm, Vertex AI, Amazon Bedrock) that integrate retrievers, generators, and external tools/APIs, but does not propose how tool/skill descriptions are indexed.
index_content_separation: N/A (survey; no index-vs-content separation mechanism of its own). It notes LlamaIndex's Agentic Document Workflows use a meta-agent with sub-agents managing smaller document sets coordinated by a top-level agent, but this is reviewed, not a contribution.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A (survey). It reviews tool/framework integration (LangChain/LangGraph, LlamaIndex, CrewAI, AG2/AutoGen, OpenAI Swarm, Semantic Kernel, Vertex AI, Amazon Bedrock) and function-calling/tool-use patterns, but does not center a live-synchronized tool index or a specific integration protocol such as MCP/RapidAPI (the v4 revision predates deep MCP coverage in its taxonomy).
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A (survey). It discusses tool use and orchestrator-workers/multi-agent task delegation at a high level but does not center an inter-tool dependency-graph retrieval formalism.
how_retrieved_used: N/A as a method. The survey describes how Agentic RAG uses retrieved content: prompt/context augmentation for LLM synthesis (data integration and LLM synthesis into a coherent response), iterative refinement of context across reflection loops, and feeding validated/refined information to a response-synthesis agent. No utilization method is implemented by the survey.
planning_integration: N/A as a method. Planning is reviewed as one of the four core agentic design patterns. The survey catalogs how retrieval interfaces with planning/acting via agentic workflow patterns: prompt chaining (sequential steps), routing (directing inputs to specialized processes), parallelization (concurrent execution), orchestrator-workers (dynamic task delegation), and evaluator-optimizer (iterative refinement). It also reviews single-agent router, multi-agent, hierarchical (tiered), corrective, adaptive, and graph-based integrations rather than committing to one.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: N/A (survey). It contrasts single-step/sequential pipelines, iterative corrective loops (per-evaluation re-retrieval), per-step multi-agent delegation, and reflection-driven refinement as surveyed interleaving styles rather than fixing one granularity.
adaptation_mechanism: N/A (not a CBR method; no retrieved-case adaptation mechanism of its own).
retrieved_item_representation: N/A (survey). Surveyed Agentic RAG injects retrieved content as natural-language documents/passages, structured query results (SQL), web snippets, and knowledge-graph subgraphs/relational structures (graph-based variants); the survey injects nothing itself.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: N/A (survey). Surveyed units range from raw documents/passages and structured records to relational graph structures; in graph-based Agentic RAG the unit is a more abstract relational/symbolic subgraph. The survey reviews this spectrum rather than fixing an abstraction level.
noise_robustness_mechanism: N/A (survey contributes none). It reviews noise/robustness mechanisms in surveyed systems: Corrective RAG's relevance-evaluation agent that filters low-relevance documents and triggers corrective re-retrieval, reflection/self-correction loops, and notes 'robustness under noisy retrieval' as a needed evaluation axis and 'retrieval quality remains the primary bottleneck' as a key lesson.
memory_type: Survey-level: it treats memory as a distinguishing capability of Agentic RAG vs Traditional RAG -- context maintenance 'enabled through memory modules' and state maintained across multi-step workflows (episodic/workflow memory). It reviews short-term context plus longer-term agent memory (e.g., CrewAI's 'robust memory systems') but, as an artifact, the survey itself has no memory. Memory management/long-term adaptation is flagged as an open research challenge.
write_back: N/A as a method. Surveyed Agentic RAG systems DO maintain/update memory and state across multi-step workflows (memory modules; CrewAI memory systems; LlamaIndex ADW maintaining state), but the survey itself stores nothing.
online_growth: N/A as a method. Surveyed agent memory grows/updates online during multi-step workflows and deployment, but the survey itself has no growing store; it raises long-term memory growth (persistence vs adaptability, knowledge drift) as an open challenge.
write_back_trigger: N/A (survey; no write-back trigger of its own). Surveyed memory updates occur per-step/per-workflow as agents maintain context; the survey discusses the open question of when to update (frequent updates can amplify hallucinations; persistent memory risks knowledge drift) without standardizing a trigger.
failure_experience_usage: N/A (survey). It reviews reflection and corrective/evaluator-optimizer patterns that act on poor or failed retrieval/outputs (relevance-evaluation triggering corrective steps), implying use of failure signals in surveyed systems, but contributes no explicit failure-experience storage scheme.
memory_evolution_update: N/A (survey). It discusses memory persistence vs. updating as an open challenge (selective retention, reconciling external knowledge with stored agent experiences, avoiding bias reinforcement/knowledge drift) but proposes no single post-write update policy.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: N/A (survey). Surveyed retrieval control is mostly agent/LLM-driven or classifier-based (Adaptive RAG's query-complexity classifier; Corrective RAG's relevance evaluator) rather than an RL-optimized retrieval policy; the survey does not center retrieval-as-learned-policy.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: Surveyed (not a method contribution): multi-agent and hierarchical Agentic RAG, orchestrator-workers, and multi-agent frameworks (CrewAI, AG2/AutoGen, OpenAI Swarm) involve coordination and shared context/state across multiple agents; it reviews rather than implements cross-agent sharing, and flags agent coordination/control and emergent behavior as an open challenge.
benchmarks: N/A as original experiments (survey reports no results of its own). It catalogs benchmarks/datasets used to evaluate RAG systems: BEIR, MS MARCO, TREC (Deep Learning Track), MuSiQue, 2WikiMultihopQA, HotpotQA, Natural Questions (NQ), TriviaQA, SQuAD, WebQ, PopQA, ELI5, NarrativeQA, ASQA, QMSum, Qasper, COVID-QA, plus Agentic/graph-RAG-specific benchmarks AgentG (Agent-G knowledge fusion) and GNN-RAG, and evaluation toolkits/benchmarks RAGBench (100,000 examples, TRACe framework), BERGEN, and FlashRAG.
benchmark_family: Survey-level grouping (Table 4 'Downstream Tasks and Datasets'): QA -- single-hop (NQ, TriviaQA, SQuAD, WebQ, PopQA, MS MARCO), multi-hop (HotpotQA, 2WikiMultihopQA, MuSiQue), long-form (ELI5, NarrativeQA, ASQA, QMSum), domain-specific (Qasper, COVID-QA); information retrieval (BEIR, MS MARCO, TREC); graph/knowledge-graph QA (Agent-G/AgentG, GNN-RAG); plus RAG evaluation frameworks/toolkits (RAGBench, BERGEN, FlashRAG). It does not use the agentic-trajectory benchmark families (web/embodied/tool/code/memory/decision-RL) as a primary axis.
baselines: N/A (survey; no method comparison/baselines of its own). Its qualitative comparison contrasts paradigm classes -- Traditional/Naive RAG vs Advanced RAG vs Modular RAG vs Graph RAG vs Agentic RAG -- and architecture classes (single-agent router, multi-agent, hierarchical/tiered, corrective, adaptive, graph-based, agentic document workflows), but runs no head-to-head experiments.
key_metrics: N/A (survey; reports no quantitative metrics of its own). It discusses that evaluation should move beyond output-level metrics (answer correctness, retrieval accuracy) toward process-aware metrics (reasoning trajectories, planning depth, adaptability, robustness under noisy retrieval, cost efficiency, tool-usage patterns).
headline_result: N/A (survey; no headline number). Its central contributions are conceptual: a principled taxonomy of Agentic RAG architectures organized by agent cardinality, control structure, knowledge representation, knowledge dependency, reasoning mode/depth, retrieval adaptivity, scalability, latency, and engineering complexity (Table 3), plus the RAG-evolution narrative (Naive -> Advanced -> Modular -> Graph -> Agentic RAG) and a Traditional-RAG vs Agentic-RAG vs Agentic-Document-Workflows comparison (Table 2). It is a widely cited preprint (Semantic Scholar: 311 citations).
ablations: N/A (survey; conducts no experiments and therefore reports no component ablations). Its closest analogue is a qualitative taxonomy-driven trade-off analysis (Table 3) mapping architecture classes to dimensions/trade-offs (e.g., single-agent = low latency but limited multi-domain reasoning; multi-agent = high scalability but coordination overhead; hierarchical/corrective = higher reliability at higher latency; graph-based = strong relational reasoning but sensitive to graph quality).
evaluation_decoupling: N/A as original measurement (survey performs no evaluation). It explicitly catalogs retrieval-focused benchmarks (BEIR, MS MARCO, TREC) separately from end-to-end RAG/QA benchmarks and toolkits (RAGBench/TRACe, BERGEN, FlashRAG), and argues intrinsic retrieval accuracy alone is insufficient, recommending decoupled process- vs outcome-level evaluation.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Survey-level: a recurring thesis (Lesson 10.5 and Challenge 12.2) is that evaluation must account for PROCESS, not just outcomes -- output-level metrics (answer correctness, retrieval accuracy) are insufficient, and process-aware metrics (reasoning efficiency/trajectories, planning depth, tool-usage patterns, adaptability to changing context, robustness under noisy retrieval) are needed. The survey itself scores nothing.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: N/A as original measurement (no cost numbers of its own). It repeatedly discusses cost/efficiency qualitatively: Agentic RAG introduces coordination complexity, latency, and computational cost (Lesson 10.1); Table 3 maps latency/scalability/engineering-complexity per architecture (single-agent = low latency; hierarchical/corrective = high latency; multi-agent = moderate latency, high scalability); and Challenge 12.4 calls for cost-aware planning, adaptive inference, selective tool invocation, and dynamic adjustment of active agents and retrieval depth.
context_budget_and_selection_count: N/A (survey; no token budget or k of its own). It discusses adaptive retrieval depth (Adaptive RAG selecting no-retrieval/single-step/multi-step by query complexity; optimizing retrieval depth based on task complexity in Challenge 12.4) as a budget lever, but prescribes no fixed-k or token budget.
survey_scope_and_axes: Primary organizing axes: (1) RAG-evolution narrative -- Naive RAG -> Advanced RAG -> Modular RAG -> Graph RAG -> Agentic RAG; (2) core agentic design patterns -- reflection, planning, tool use, multi-agent collaboration; (3) agentic workflow patterns -- prompt chaining, routing, parallelization, orchestrator-workers, evaluator-optimizer; (4) a principled architecture taxonomy by agent cardinality (single vs multiple vs tiered), control structure (centralized/flat/hierarchical/adaptive), autonomy, and knowledge representation (unstructured/hybrid/graph-based/document-centric) -- instantiated as single-agent router, multi-agent, hierarchical, corrective, adaptive, graph-based (Agent-G, GeAR), and agentic document workflows; (5) applications (customer support, healthcare, legal, finance, education, multimodal/graph-enhanced); (6) tools/frameworks; (7) lessons learned; and (8) open challenges (coordination, evaluation, memory, cost/efficiency, safety/governance, generalization). Coverage window ~2024-2026 (v1 Jan 2025, v4 Apr 2026); references ~71 (Semantic Scholar referenceCount) up to ~127 distinct bibliography entries cited in the v4 HTML. [uncertain] exact final reference count varies by version.
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (this is a survey, not a benchmark; it constructs no dataset). It does report sizes for benchmarks it catalogs, e.g., RAGBench is described as a large-scale explainable benchmark with 100,000 examples using the TRACe framework, and BEIR as spanning 17 datasets.
builds_on: Builds on and synthesizes the RAG literature (Lewis et al. RAG; Gao et al. 'Retrieval-Augmented Generation for LLMs: A Survey' for the Naive/Advanced/Modular taxonomy and the downstream-task/dataset table) and the Graph RAG line; on agentic-pattern literature (reflection, planning, tool use, multi-agent collaboration) and Anthropic-style agentic workflow patterns (prompt chaining, routing, parallelization, orchestrator-workers, evaluator-optimizer); on specific Agentic RAG variants it reviews (Corrective RAG/CRAG, Adaptive-RAG by query complexity, Agent-G and GeAR for graph-based, GNN-RAG); and on frameworks (LangChain/LangGraph, LlamaIndex ADW, CrewAI, AG2/AutoGen, OpenAI Swarm, Semantic Kernel, Vertex AI, Amazon Bedrock). It aggregates these rather than extending a single predecessor method.
contrasts_with: Positions Agentic RAG explicitly against Traditional/Naive RAG (static workflows, limited context, poor multi-step reasoning), Advanced RAG, Modular RAG, and Graph RAG, arguing agents add adaptability, multi-step reasoning, and dynamic retrieval management (Table 2). Notably it tempers this (Lesson 10.1): Agentic RAG is NOT always the right default -- for simple fact retrieval, modular RAG is sufficient with lower overhead. As a survey it complements other RAG/agent surveys (e.g., Gao et al.'s RAG survey, which it adapts for its dataset table).
lineage: Surveys group. A flagship 2025 Agentic RAG survey providing a principled architecture taxonomy (agent cardinality, control structure, autonomy, knowledge representation) and a RAG-evolution narrative. It serves as an umbrella reference for the retrieval-augmented-agent sub-topics -- particularly multi-agent/agentic retrieval, corrective/adaptive retrieval, and graph-based retrieval (relevant to groups B, C, and E in this collection) -- rather than being a method within any single sub-topic.
